data.description:
## Symptom

Three separate repo gates are enforced by pytest but **not** by `make lint`, so a contributor who runs
the documented pre-flight gets a green result and learns otherwise only from a Gerrit `Verified -1`,
15–20 minutes later:

| gate | what it catches | how it surfaced |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` | a new mechanism that `--check` admitted via a `mechanism-ok` marker but the baseline does not contain | change 2601 pushed red; `make lint` was exit 0 |
| `tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` | a CI step that cannot run on a tree predating it | change 2600 pushed red; caught only in CI |
| `tests/unit/test_api_surface_gate.py` | public API surface drift vs the committed baseline | change 2609 pushed red; `make lint` was exit 0 |

All three fired on real changes on 2026-09-04, and in each case the author had run `make lint` and
`make typecheck` and seen them pass.

## Why this matters more than the individual failures

The cost is not the CI round-trip alone. It is that **`make lint` is the documented contract**:
AGENTS.md points contributors at it as the commit gate, the pre-commit hook runs it, and agents are
briefed to treat it as the local proxy for CI. A proxy that returns green for a tree CI will reject
is worse than no proxy, because it converts "I verified locally" into a false statement made in good
faith. Three agents made exactly that statement tonight.

There is a related trap in the same family, worth fixing alongside: `test_predates_gate_guard_parity`
considers only **git-tracked** paths. A change that adds a new file and runs the gate *before*
`git add` gets a green that flips to red the moment the file is staged. That is a second way the
local signal disagrees with CI on an unchanged tree.

## Not a request to move everything into `make lint`

Some of these are genuinely test-shaped and belong in the suite; `make lint` running the full pytest
tier would be far too slow to be a commit gate, which is presumably why they live where they do. The
defect is the **contract**, not the placement. Any of these resolves it:

- a fast `make check-gates` (or an addition to `make lint`) that runs exactly these ratchet/parity
  tests and nothing else — they are quick; the three together run in well under a minute; **or**
- `make lint` invoking them directly, if that stays fast enough to remain a commit gate; **or**
- if they must stay separate, AGENTS.md stating explicitly that `make lint` is NOT sufficient and
  naming the full set a contributor must run before pushing.

The third is the weakest — documentation does not fail a build — but it is honest, and honest beats a
green that lies.

## Acceptance criteria

Deterministic, verifiable in one run.

1. A single documented command verifies everything CI will check that is checkable locally. Running
   it on a tree that violates any of the three gates above fails; running it on a clean tree passes.
2. Demonstrated per gate: introduce a violation of each of the three in turn, show the command going
   RED, and revert. Three RED demonstrations, quoted.
3. The `git add` skew is closed or documented: either the parity gate considers the working tree as
   CI will see it, or the command's output states that untracked files are not covered and what to do.
4. AGENTS.md names the command as the pre-push contract, replacing or supplementing the current
   `make lint` guidance so a contributor is not left inferring the set.
5. The command is portable — it must work in a checkout with no CI provider, per the blocking
   `project.portability` criterion.

## File impact

`Makefile`, `AGENTS.md`, possibly `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and
`tests/unit/test_predates_gate_guard_parity.py` for AC3.
data.title: make lint is a lying proxy for CI: three ratchet/parity gates are pytest-only, so a locally-green tree fails Verified
